summary: The bill amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to restrict asylum applications to ports of entry only, bar parole or release into the U.S. for those applicants, and eliminate eligibility for anyone apprehended after entering without inspection.

scores.thoughts: The bill makes no reference to federal spending, appropriations, or budget authority. It is a narrow amendment to asylum procedures under immigration law.
No provisions address tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue collection.
The bill contains no language related to health insurance, medical services, or healthcare delivery systems.
No provisions concern firearms, background checks, or gun regulations.

The bill directly amends INA Section 208(a) to restrict asylum eligibility to applications made only at ports of entry, prohibits parole or release into the United States for such applicants, eliminates prior exceptions allowing claims elsewhere, and bars eligibility for those apprehended after unlawful entry. These changes are explicitly designed to limit asylum claims and enforce border procedures, aligning strongly with restricting immigration pathways.
No provisions relate to reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill does not address military funding, defense policy, or armed forces.
No environmental, regulatory, or climate-related provisions are present.
The legislation does not modify welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net benefits.
No education funding, school policy, or student provisions are included.
The bill contains no references to controlled substances, decriminalization, or drug enforcement.
While the bill affects immigration enforcement, it does not alter criminal sentencing, policing standards, or rehabilitation programs; asylum is a civil immigration matter.
No trade agreements, tariffs, or import/export rules are addressed.
The bill has no fiscal impact language or debt-related provisions.
No provisions address sexual orientation, gender identity, or related legal protections.
The legislation does not mention foreign assistance, aid programs, or international funding.
No election administration, voting access, or campaign provisions are present.
The bill does not regulate technology, data collection, or privacy standards.
No labor, union, or employment regulation language appears.
The bill does not address religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or anti-discrimination rules.
